acceptance.given: The complete current Consumer Manifest and repository caller set are available for inspection.

oracle.expected: A deterministic reconciliation artifact shows a mutual, complete mapping in both directions, covering VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing callers.
forbidden: Any omitted VDD, Acceptance, or workflow-model-routing caller
Any Consumer Manifest entry left unreconciled
oracle.observable: The generated reconciliation output contains bidirectional sets with zero omissions or extras across all required caller categories.

acceptance.then: The reconciliation is accepted only when Consumer Manifest entries and repository callers match exactly in both directions.
acceptance.when: Run the repository consumer-manifest reconciliation checks against current VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing call sites.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a reconciliation case with an omitted Consumer Manifest entry or repository caller, including VDD, Acceptance, or workflow-model-routing coverage, and require the check to fail.

affected_subjects: Complete current Consumer Manifest and repository callers
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or repair bidirectional reconciliation so the complete Consumer Manifest is matched against every repository caller, explicitly including VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing consumers.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing route decision schema and consumer control behavior; rollback only reconciliation logic and its tests.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unreconciled or partial manifest state transitions to a complete bidirectionally reconciled manifest.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Reconciliation verification reports exact bidirectional equality with zero missing or extra callers across VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing categories.

acceptance.given: An invalid-package case is presented to the repository package validation evaluator.

oracle.expected: The evaluator returns a non-success result for the invalid package and does not emit a success receipt.
forbidden: A success result for an invalid package
A pass receipt authorizing the invalid package
oracle.observable: The validation process exits nonzero or otherwise records a rejected verdict for the invalid-package case.

acceptance.then: Success is rejected and the invalid package remains unapproved.
acceptance.when: Execute the package validator and its negative compatibility probe against the invalid-package fixture.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the invalid-package replay case and require failure if validation exits zero or emits a success status.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure invalid-package evaluation is fail-closed, including rejection when a validator would otherwise return success for invalid content.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep validation receipt schema and active capability contract compatible; rollback only invalid-package rejection changes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Invalid package input transitions to an explicit non-success verdict without authorization.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The invalid-package test exits nonzero and no success receipt is produced for that case.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has succeeded and contains its target, validator, dependency, command, Probe, output, Consumer, snapshot, and authority bindings.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result records an independently verified Consumer binding, with verification evidence distinct from the replay success claim.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result lacking independent Consumer verification
Consumer verification inferred solely from replay exit status
oracle.observable: Replay receipt inspection finds a separate Consumer verification record bound to the successful result.

acceptance.then: The result is accepted only when independent Consumer verification is present and valid.
acceptance.when: Run replay and inspect the emitted receipt for an independently executed or validated Consumer check.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a successful replay receipt with its Consumer verification removed or mismatched and require the acceptance check to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Emit and validate an independent Consumer verification binding on every successful Replay Result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve replay receipt fields and authorizes=[] semantics while allowing additive independent Consumer verification evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Successful replay transitions to independently consumer-verified success; missing or invalid verification remains rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Replay integration checks pass only when the receipt contains independently verified Consumer evidence bound to the same result.

acceptance.given: A native command identity exists before repair and a post-repair identity record is available.

oracle.expected: Before/after comparison shows the native command identity is byte-for-byte unchanged.
forbidden: Any replacement of the native command
Any changed executable, argument binding, or command identity
oracle.observable: The identity comparison artifact reports equality for the native command before and after repair.

acceptance.then: Repair is accepted only if native command identity remains unchanged.
acceptance.when: During repair validation, compare the recorded native command identity with the post-repair command identity using the repository command/replay checks.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a repair variant that changes the native command identity and require the identity comparison guard to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve the native command identity across repair and reject any drift in executable or argument binding.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema or lifecycle changes; rollback only command-identity guard implementation.

slice_hint.state_transition: Existing native command identity remains stable through repair; drift transitions to rejected repair.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The before/after identity comparison passes only on exact equality and fails on any command replacement or mutation.
